title: Microsoft SQL Server Quick Guide
description: Find a short explanation and a worked example for each idea in the Microsoft SQL Server course.

entries.name: Calculate a named answer
entries.summary: T-SQL SELECT can return a calculation. AS gives the output column a name that explains the answer.

entries.name: Keep a local variable
entries.summary: A T-SQL variable starts with @. DECLARE gives it a type and an optional starting value.

example.code:
DECLARE @name nvarchar(40)=N'Mia';
SELECT N'Hello, '+@name AS greeting;

entries.name: Make a table variable
entries.summary: A table variable holds a small set of rows inside a batch.

entries.name: Choose top rows with a clear order
entries.summary: TOP limits the returned rows. ORDER BY tells SQL Server which rows count as first.

entries.name: Filter rows with two rules
entries.summary: WHERE can combine tests with AND. A row must pass both tests to be included.

entries.name: Summarise groups
entries.summary: GROUP BY collects rows with the same category.

entries.name: Read related tables
entries.summary: A join matches rows by keys. The relationship should be explicit instead of relying on row order.

entries.name: Handle a conversion that may fail
entries.summary: TRY_CAST attempts a type conversion. It returns NULL when an ordinary conversion fails, so code can handle the missing result.

example.code:
SELECT TRY_CAST(N'12' AS int) AS good_value,
       TRY_CAST(N'twelve' AS int) AS missing_value;

entries.name: Number a sorted result
entries.summary: ROW_NUMBER assigns a sequence based on its window order.

entries.name: Undo a sample transaction
entries.summary: A transaction can keep related changes together.

entries.name: Pass a query parameter
entries.summary: A parameter keeps a data value separate from the SQL command text.

entries.name: Let an identity column make an id
entries.summary: An IDENTITY column generates numeric values for new rows.
